name: openplanet-lsp-vscode
description: Language support for Openplanet AngelScript plugins (openplanet-lsp wrapper)

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The language server analyzes workspace files and openplanetLsp.serverPath executes a configured binary. File contents are sent to the server process.

openplanetLsp.serverPath.description: Absolute path to the openplanet-lsp binary. Leave empty to use the bundled binary (when available) or the first `openplanet-lsp` on PATH.

openplanetLsp.openplanetDir.markdownDescription: Path to the Openplanet installation directory (auto-detected when empty). When set, forwarded to the server as `openplanet_dir` — overrides `.openplanet-lsp.toml`.

openplanetLsp.pluginsDir.markdownDescription: Path to the Openplanet plugins directory (auto-detected when empty). When set, forwarded to the server as `plugins_dir` — overrides `.openplanet-lsp.toml`.

openplanetLsp.gameTarget.markdownDescription: Which game the LSP compiles `#if` platform branches for (preprocessor defines). `TMNEXT` = Trackmania (2020). Leave at default to let a workspace `.openplanet-lsp.toml` decide. Changing this restarts the server.

enumDescriptions: All four signature defines (SIG_OFFICIAL, SIG_REGULAR, SIG_SCHOOL, SIG_DEVELOPER) — what an unsigned/dev-mode plugin compiles with. Server default.
openplanetLsp.signatureMode.markdownDescription: Which signature level's `SIG_*` defines are live. Openplanet defines a signature macro when the current level is equal or **below** that macro's level, so the levels are cumulative — set this to check your plugin the way it compiles once signed (`#if SIG_DEVELOPER` blocks go dead below `developer`). Forwarded to the server as `signature_mode`; left at `developer` nothing is sent, so a workspace `.openplanet-lsp.toml` keeps control. Changing this restarts the server.

openplanetLsp.defines.markdownDescription: Extra preprocessor defines, **added** to the ones the game target and signature level derive and to `info.toml` `[script].defines` — listing `DEV` does not drop `TMNEXT`. Prefix an entry with `-` or `!` to turn a define off (`-LOGS`). Forwarded to the server as `defines`.

enumDescriptions: Unset — the workspace .openplanet-lsp.toml or the user config decides (server default: warn).
Turn the unused-declaration pass off entirely.
Report as Hints: greyed out in the editor, kept out of the Problems panel.
Report as Infos: greyed out in the editor and listed in the Problems panel.
Report as Errors, so `openplanet-lsp check` fails on them.
openplanetLsp.unused.markdownDescription: How unused functions / variables / parameters / class members are reported. `hint` and `info` report the same findings at a quieter severity and never fail a `check`, not even under `--warnings-as-errors`. Findings are tagged `Unnecessary` at every level, so the declaration is faded in the editor regardless (see `editor.showUnused`). Forwarded to the server as `unused`; left empty nothing is sent, so a workspace `.openplanet-lsp.toml` keeps control. Changing this restarts the server.

enumDescriptions: Unset — the workspace .openplanet-lsp.toml or the user config decides (server default: hint).
Do not mark inactive branches at all.
Grey the dead branch out in the editor, without listing it in the Problems panel.
Grey the dead branch out and list it in the Problems panel.
openplanetLsp.inactiveRegions.markdownDescription: Grey out `#if` branches that the current preprocessor defines switch off, the way an IDE fades `#if 0` in C. Forwarded to the server as `inactive_regions`; left empty nothing is sent, so a workspace `.openplanet-lsp.toml` keeps control. There is deliberately no warning/error level: a branch that is off for your target is dead by design, not a defect, and `openplanet-lsp check` never reports these at all. The fade needs `editor.showUnused` (on by default). Changing this restarts the server.

openplanetLsp.pluginRoots.markdownDescription: Directories containing an `info.toml` (plugin roots), absolute or workspace-relative. When non-empty, forwarded to the server as `plugin_roots` and it **replaces** the server's automatic downward workspace scan. When empty/unset nothing is forwarded and the server auto-discovers plugin roots by scanning the workspace.
